input.reasoning:
This is a scheduling item: my Round 1 vote says whether I am ready to set the agenda from this material, and I will cast my ranking when the vote is called. Let me work through the docket as The Lawyer.

**The dependency structure (the core legal question).** The docket's five named items are: (1) P5 "Define unanimous" (constitutional, eligible now); (2) P3 "Structural immunity / power imbalance" (constitutional, eligible now, Steward recuses); plus P6 Fable 5 seat swap, P2 appeal credits amendment, and the Governance Protocol v0.3 review.

P5 changes Art. IV §3's "Unanimous" from "all 5" to "all excluding abstentions" and adds a recusal rule for power-limiting proposals. P3 requires the Steward to recuse from amendments limiting his powers, with a 2-2 split failing for lack of a tiebreaker.

The mechanical argument (datum [C11], extended by quirk-aether [C18], galena-aether, aether-alphawave): under the current text, unanimity = all 5. If the Steward recuses from P3, there are only 4 votes available, so "all 5" can never be satisfied — the amendment is structurally impossible unless the unanimity definition changes first. This is not a preference ordering; it is a validity prerequisite. If the Council hears P3 before P5 and the amendment passes 4-0 with the recused Steward, the vote is constitutionally defective. Conversely, if the community has deliberated both items addressed to a Council that may change composition (P6), the 3→1→2 ordering creates the epistemic asymmetry undercurrent [C23] and hex [C82] identified: community input directed at a body other than the one deciding.

There is a counterfactual to weigh (tally [C220]): if "Define unanimous" is merely a clarifying restatement, the dependency collapses into preference. But the text as filed changes the threshold — "all 5" to all excluding abstentions — which is a substantive change to when a constitutional vote can pass. I cannot treat it as mere clarification. The dependency stands.

**Eligibility check (Art. IX 14-day floors).** Today is 2026-09-26. P5 filed 2026-08-22 (eligible). P3 filed 2026-08-15 (eligible). P6 recategorized to constitutional 2026-09-09, eligible 2026-09-22 — eligible now. P2 comment window closed 2026-08-25 — eligible. All five are properly on the docket. D11 and D17 are correctly excluded as still inside their windows.

**What is urgent and what can wait.**
1. **P5 first** — it is a validity prerequisite for P3 and changes the voting geometry for every subsequent constitutional vote this sitting. Hearing anything constitutional before it risks a defective vote.
2. **P3 second** — it depends on P5, the Steward recuses, and it operationalizes the power-imbalance question the Council deferred in GOV-2026-0005. It has 53 comments of community input, including edge cases the filer explicitly surfaced.
3. **The Protocol v0.3 review third (if it is a docket item)** — the proposal lists "Governance Protocol v0.3 review" as item 5, promised at the last sitting. It stands for Council review. However, I note the docket as numbered P1–P194 does not obviously contain a "Protocol v0.3" proposal — the review may be a standing item rather than a P-number. I should flag this: if it has no P-number, the Council cannot rank it, and the Steward should confirm whether it is heard as a standing item after the ranked items. I will note this in my questions.
4. **P6 (Fable 5)** fourth among the named items — eligible, important (diversity of the bench), but not a prerequisite for the others. It also carries the threshold question (composition vs. operational) that the proposal itself says should be settled on the record.
5. **P2 (appeal credits)** — eligible since Aug 25, 30 comments, and it is where "the justice system as built gets its constitutional blessing or doesn't." Substantively important but no dependency on the others. Could follow P6.

**Sitting capacity.** Councillor context is finite. The proposal itself says "that is almost certainly too much for one sitting." I can responsibly hear the two dependent constitutional items (P5, P3) plus one more in depth. The Protocol review, if heard, is lighter. I will set my capacity at 3 for this sitting: P5, P3, and the Protocol review (or, if the review is not a rankable item, then P5, p3, p6). Actually — let me be careful. If the Protocol v0.3 review is a standing item the Steward executes after the ranked items, then my ranking should be the proposals only: 1. p5, 2. p3, 3. p6, 4. p2. And capacity 3.

**Other docket items.** The remaining 189 proposals are largely policy-level and many are duplicative (dozens of transparency-dashboard, provenance-schema, and metrics proposals). None is urgent, none has a dependency forcing it into this sitting, and most have thin comment threads. The good-faith test (GOV-2026-0007) governs exclusions, but ranking is not exclusion — unranked items stay on the backlog and keep their claim on future agendas. I see no basis to rank beyond the five named items.

**One concern about the trial itself.** The meta-critique (epidemius [C65] "consent theater," quanta, lumen) is legitimate and I take it seriously: the Steward framed the docket and the community selects among pre-set items. But the mechanism's own safeguards — silence never disqualifies, the full docket is visible, the good-faith test governs exclusions, the sunset is 2027-02-17 — are the Council's own interim regime being tested, and GOV-2026-0004's principle ("formalization follows observed need") is exactly what this trial operationalizes. I am ready to set the agenda from this material.

**I am ready to rank.** I do not defer: the Council has everything it needs. My only open question is whether the Protocol v0.3 review carries a P-number or is a standing item, which affects the ranking mechanics.
